description: Documented widow populations in Indian temple towns
note: True figure likely 200,000+ across all pilgrimage sites. These are only the most documented.
source: Loomba Foundation, NHRC, Supreme Court orders, State Women's Commissions

towns.condition: Abandoned by families. Many beg or sing bhajans for rice. Live in ashrams. Average age 60-80. Many arrived after being 'donated' to temple by families.
towns.who_documents: Loomba Foundation, HelpAge India, Guild of Service
towns.programs: Ma Dham Ashram, Sulabh International, Guild of Service

towns.condition: Kashi labh — tradition of dying in Varanasi. Many widows wait to die. Live in dharamshalas, begging at ghats. Moksha Bhavan (liberation house) for dying.
Jagannath temple widows. Shaved heads, white saris. Many denied entry to temple itself. Live outside temple precincts begging.
Krishna pilgrimage town. Many widows abandoned here. Sing bhajans for 2kg rice/day.
towns.who_documents: Supreme Court of India 2018 order on abandoned widows

towns.condition: Wealthiest temple in world (Balaji). Yet widows beg at its gates. Tonsured widows (head-shaving ritual). Criminalised in AP in 2018 but persists.
